Giberd (A81)

Verified 2026-10-13 · local Mod v1.37.5.0 · English scoring region: Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

Story quality: High; primarily based on local flavour text | Mission-tree length: 36 direct missions | Update context: current installed v1.37.5.0; the actual final authoring date was not independently established | Distinctiveness: High; three faction influences, elections, and research rewards interact rather than forming three permanent endings | Waiting burden (lower is smoother): Medium; diplomacy, research, and event-state gates matter | Opening pressure: 66/100, not an in-game difficulty test | Expansion demand: 72/100, pushed by both war and development

v2.1: Expansion 74 · Autocracy 45 · Magic/Artifice direction 20 · Theme intensity 94 · Pluralism 62; value profile: Good (68), trajectory branch-dependent. These five axes are not a four-letter type; route profiles are kept separately in the v2.2 conditional portrait.

Overview for the player

Giberd is a free city where gnomish research, commerce, and imperial politics share the same table. You must secure room and influence while managing three domestic factions with different positions on technology, institutions, and religious groups. Artificery is not a side bonus: it is the axis of research, maintenance, and political competition. It suits players who enjoy dense internal politics and institutional experiments. War matters, but the real story is how a city becomes strong enough to shape an empire.

Historical setting and the 1444 situation

【Wiki supplement】The English offline page places Giberd in the imperial gnome environment of Esmaria and records a background of refugees and knowledge exchange after the Dragonwake. This is world-lore context, not enough to establish a precise chronology by itself, and it does not allow later mission content to be rewritten as institutions already present at the founding.

【Established local identity】In 1444 Giberd is a Free City republic with Imperial Gnomish culture, the Regent Court, the Gnomish technology group, capital 271, and 25 mercantilism; Silverforge is listed as a historical friend. Delda enters the history from 1399 as a long-lived female ruler. The three domestic faction variables begin at zero, the Artificer organisation is locked, and the opening event sets the country to mixed magic-and-artifice mode.

An imperial-candidate flag represents a political storyline or qualification, not a claim that this Free City already holds the imperial crown. Missions that pursue imperial influence are future ambitions and must not be projected backward onto the opening identity.

Distinctive mechanics and campaign rhythm

Giberd's internal competition centres on Technomancers, the Brillites, and the Mechanists. Influence accumulation interacts with elections, leader rewards, and later events. A normal candidate grants different values, but that does not mean every election changes the country's civilizational direction. The central challenge is balancing research, finance, and factions until later institutions make those accumulated choices matter more.

The missions also require dealing with Konwell, Esmaria, commercial shipping, and imperial affairs. Diplomacy and commerce are not side branches of research: the city needs resources, space, and political standing before research can become state capacity. Artificer development and maintenance have concrete state conditions; mission prose about research does not mean inventions are free clicks.

The God Fragment missions illustrate the loop. They require access to province 898 together with the relevant invention research, maintenance, and use conditions, then provide a faction-wide modifier and an event entry point. The 36 directly counted missions therefore form a connected campaign of research, external influence, and internal integration rather than a peaceful building checklist.

Mission future and major policy choices

【Mission future】The Ravellian group and the God Fragment make the later question more than how to build faster. The dedicated event flavor_giberd.39 explicitly presents three positions: Technomancers support full Ravellian entry into government and cultural-academic participation; the Brillites allow participation but place Ravellians below artificers; the Mechanists oppose their entry into guilds and the state machine.

Under the current scoring boundary, these are reversible policies rather than permanently exclusive endings. Future elections can change the policy. The direct event effects are faction influence and leader rewards, and do not by themselves establish an eternal citizenship law. The three conditional portraits mainly change the pluralist-integration axis; their shared research goals, urban development, and imperial ambition remain.

The archive event also has options to repair, strip research, or relocate the institution. The current evidence establishes an institutional and resource decision; faction rewards in research, language, or intimidation do not automatically create three permanent civilizational personalities. The article preserves those differences without turning every bonus option into a national ending.

National personality and values

The production baseline shows strong external goals, distributed political competition, a pronounced artificery direction, and high thematic intensity. Its baseline pluralism does not average the two policy extremes; it represents the common national profile. The separate v2.2 route portraits record the conditional Ravellian choices and do not automatically replace the production matcher.

The value profile sits at the lower edge of Good, based on research for the public good, commerce, and institution-building rather than on republican government alone. A policy that restricts Ravellian participation must be assessed as group treatment; this batch does not establish enslavement, purges, or total religious extermination. Imperial expansion, artificery intensity, and the existence of imperial-candidate politics do not independently determine moral value.

Development context, community, and cautions

【Development context】The 2024 Official Dev Diary #62, “Talking Cannor Content,” introduces the country's newer content and supports its design context at that time. Other logs only mention older reform context and are not treated as new Giberd history. 【Community view】Player discussions from 2024 and 2026 emphasise the transition from a gnomish city into imperial politics, commerce, and high-intensity artificery; their version differences do not erase current conditions or DLC limits.

Giberd is recommended for players who enjoy faction management, research, and imperial diplomacy working together. If you do not want to manage invention states, maintenance, and several lines of development, the mission density can become a burden. The map shows the actual 1444 starting position, not a future imperial domain. The three policy portraits likewise do not promise that one route remains available in every version.

See the evidence page for source files, fixed Wiki revisions, and unresolved boundaries. The English translation receipt is bilingual-v235-text-A81-review.md.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Racial, government and mission rewards are excluded. Successor ideas do not automatically stack with predecessor ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, not automatically events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Inherited effect values and unresolved units remain qualified without changing Chinese source data.

Giberd (A81) — Giberdi Ideas

Traditions: Giberdi Traditions

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%; State maintenance: -25%.

Idea 1: Exiles of the Dragonwake

A thousand years ago our ancestors lived in the Gnomish Newlands under the banners of the glorious Gnomish Hierarchy, when the Dragons awoke, causing countless kobolds to rise up and destroy many of our cities and forcing us to flee from what is now called the 'Dragon Coast'. We spent centuries wandering from country to country until we finally settled in Esmaria. Of course, during our migration we learned how to efficiently move a large group of people through the countryside...

Effects: global_manpower_modifier：+15%.

Idea 2: Esmari Influences

We have been in Esmaria for centuries, in that time it is only natural that we adopted some of the customs of our saviours, including their religion. To make our ties with our neighbours even stronger, Giberd can also count a bustling human minority as part of its citizenry, with them being able to elect representatives for the city council. We are as Esmari as anyone.

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +200%.

Idea 3: Institution of the Gibing Day

No day is of greater importance to a Giberdi gnome then Gibing Day. The festival has occurred since the day Giberd was founded, repeating on the same day every year since. The festival starts with the ringing of church bells as denizens gather in their town squares; from there, a human is randomly selected from the crowd to play the role of the King of Esmaria and a gnome to play the gnomish delegate. Each signs a small piece of paper, reflecting the historical transfer of Giberd to the gnomes. They then initiate the first dance together, gnomes pairing up with humans in a grand circle around the two actors, gnome arms linked with human as the celebrations continue.

Finally, a feast is prepared in the town centre, with a mix of traditional gnomish & Esmari dishes. All partake in the feast and watch from the river the passing of a procession of gnomish ships. These decorative ships are rebuilt and floated each year, to commemorate how the gnomish refugees entered Giberd and called it home.

Effects: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 4: Giberd Civil Engineering Academy

When people mention the gnomes, the first thing that comes to their minds is our craftsmanship. Though our permanence in Esmaria has modified our way of life, we still have our skills. Recently, though, there have been cities which, thanks to the riches of the new world, have expanded greatly. Some of the gnomish scholars in Konwell have returned with the idea to institute a dedicated urbanistic engineering academy which will serve us well in keeping up with the rest of the world.

Effects: Development cost: -10%; Build time: -15%.

Idea 5: Golden Giberdi

The drink of choice of the river parties for more than a hundred years, Golden Giberdi is the peak of luxurious liquor. Sold in a gnome-shaped bottle expertly crafted by Giberdi glassblowers and wrapped in decadent gold leaf from the minted gold coins of the Empire of Anbennar, it fetches a premium at home and abroad. Lapping luxury from the tip of the gnome's hat, which softly uncorks to reveal the luscious liquid inside, few will be left standing after a glass or two of this beautiful booze. While some may claim that the high alcohol content of Golden Giberdi is the prime reason so many accidents occur at our river parties, Glibgear’s Golden Brewery laugh at such petty calumny. So pour a glass of Golden Giberdi fast and steer your party in the right direction.

Effects: Number of merchants: +1.

Idea 6: The Perilous Grounds

The discoveries brought home from Aelantir truly changed the world as we know it, from religion to, of course, technology. Some of our adventurers brought home several 'souvenirs' from the ancestral home of the elves, and those souvenirs are the joy of our engineers, who have basically gone crazy with experiments. By setting a desolated area dedicated to these experiments, we may at least not destroy our city, we may at least protect our city from their mad machinations.

Effects: Production efficiency: +15%.

Idea 7: Artificer Loading Exoskeleton V1

Gnomes aren't renowned for their physical prowess. We always had to use over encumbering machinery to lift weights that humans are able to lift with their bare hands, and they too have limits, not wanting to work all day long like all gnomes. Our master engineers, though, have finally developed an exoskeleton that can be worn by gnomes, maybe even making larger ones for our human companions, that make us able to lift and transport cargo that we didn't even think was able to be moved in the first place.

Effects: Trade steering: +15%.

Ambition: Giberdi Ambition

Effects: Global trade power: +20%.
